qt: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Marco Zanni (ID) Subject:

On Friday 19 January, during a speech at the University of Valladolid, the Vice-President of the Commission/High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Josep Borrell stated that Hamas had been financed by the State of Israel to weaken the Palestinian Authority. Such statements are an affront to the integrity of Israel and to the families of the victims of the tragic attacks perpetrated by Hamas on 7 October 2023. They also risk undermining diplomatic relations between the European Union and the State of Israel, at a time when Tel Aviv needs unconditional support in waging its war against Hamas. Can the Vice-President / High Representative therefore state: 1.
On what sources and what factual evidence is he basing his claims?

Given the changing geopolitical landscape in the Middle East and the risk of escalation in the area, does he consider his statements to have been made at the appropriate time and to be compatible with the diplomatic duty entrusted to him?
at: (English version) to the Vice-President of the Commission/High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Marco Zanni (ID) (25 January 2024) Subject: Statements by the Vice-President/High Representative on Israel's financing of Hamas On Friday 19 January, during a speech at the University of Valladolid, the Vice-President of the Commission/High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Josep Borrell stated that Hamas had been financed by the State of Israel to weaken the Palestinian Authority. Such statements are an affront to the integrity of Israel and to the families of the victims of the tragic attacks perpetrated by Hamas on 7 October 2023. They also risk undermining diplomatic relations between the European Union and the State of Israel, at a time when Tel Aviv needs unconditional support in waging its war against Hamas. Can the Vice-President/High Representative therefore state: 1.
On what sources and what factual evidence is he basing his claims?

Given the changing geopolitical landscape in the Middle East and the risk of escalation in the area, does he consider his statements to have been made at the appropriate time and to be compatible with the diplomatic duty entrusted to him?

(6 August 2024) The remarks of the High Representative/Vice-President (HR/VP) are considered common knowledge in Israel and the region and are corroborated by a variety of authoritative sources, including recent statements by former Shin Beit Chiefs Ami Ayalon (1) and Yuval Diskin, former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Barak (2) and, indeed, Prime Minister Netanyahu himself (3). There is ample open-source material on the previous policy of the government of Israel to allow the transfer of funds to finance the Hamas-run authorities in Gaza (4), which is currently the subject of discussions in the Israeli political sphere. The remarks of the HR/VP were made in the context of efforts to resolve the current crisis in the Middle East, to help ensure the release of all remaining hostages and end the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, and to prevent the events on and since 7 October 2023 from ever repeating themselves. The EU remains firmly committed to lasting peace based on the two-state solution, as reaffirmed in the European Council conclusions of 27 June 2024 (5), which is the best, and only viable, guarantee for Israel’s long-term security. The HR/VP’s remarks were therefore in no way ‘an affront to the integrity of Israel and to the families of the 7 October terrorist attacks’, many of whom the HR/VP has personally engaged with on several occasions. The HR/VP spares no effort to work with regional and international partners to reduce the risk of further escalation in the region, to find a way out of the crisis, and to revive meaningful peace efforts.
